title: The fuel budget shrinks
hook: If fuel gets cheaper, would you buy more premium gasoline?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Separate a general income increase from spending inside a labeled fuel account.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Separate a general income increase from spending inside a labeled fuel account.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy household saves €20 on fuel and spends €10 of that on an upgrade. How much of the saving remains? Toy inputs A=[80, 20, 10]; B=[80, 20, 0].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[60, 10, 10, 70], [60, 20, 0, 80]]. Labels: Fuel base €, Saving left €, Upgrade €, Total left €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The fuel account’s label can organize a spending decision, but it cannot create extra income. The two allocations use the same saving; only the upgrade purchase differs. A household income effect and account-specific spending are separate comparisons.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Old budget €=80, Fuel saving €=20, Upgrade €=0. What is Saving left €? Answer: 20.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Old budget €=80, Fuel saving €=20, Upgrade €=0. What is Saving left €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 20. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: When gas prices fell, US households upgraded to premium gasoline far more than the income gain would predict (Hastings & Shapiro, 2013).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Separate a general income increase from spending inside a labeled fuel account.
